notes.title: March, April & May Update
notes.content:
Welcome to the March, April, & May 2025 update for Blue Sky Aces, a low poly WW1 flight simulator that is currently under development. The last few months have resulted in a big change in direction when it comes to map building, and we've gone back to the future with the new approach. We now have a map builder that we can start to build much larger, and far more detailed maps than ever before.

In this update I'll discuss why we changed direction, and demonstrate the new approach.

Other work discussed during this video includes:
 - Improvements to the mouse handling, especially with the simulation flight model.
 - An updated drag equation to prevent aircraft accelerating too fast.
 - More realistic handling at the edge of the flight envelope, particularly below the aircraft's stall speed.
 - And the ability to speed up time to make it more enjoyable to explore the maps.
[previewyoutube=lNCeDV0rjv8;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: January & February 2025 Update
notes.content:
Welcome to the January & February 2025 update for Blue Sky Aces, a low poly WW1 flight simulator. The last couple of months have been really busy, but I finally managed to update the demo build on Steam, which importantly includes the new simulation flight model. This had been the source of many sleepless nights during the last quarter of 2024, so it was really great to finally get it released.

In this update we show off two new aircraft, the Fokker DVI and the Royal Aircraft Factory Se5a. As part of this work we've also worked to improve the in cockpit animations for the weapons.

Other work discussed during this video includes:
 - Improvements to the bullet hole rendering.
 - Fixes to the aircraft AI.
 - Map building from GIS data.

[previewyoutube=0CW-ZBWjG1s;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Demo Update - 0.86.41
notes.content:
The version 0.86.41 demo update addresses various minor issues with the aircraft AI such as:
[list]
[*] Their tendency to always fly at very low altitudes when being attacked.
[*] The problem where they would fire continuous bursts of fire that would jam their guns, leaving them unable to attack for long periods of time.
[*] Improvements have been done to make them better at aiming at higher deflection angles.
[*] They would sometimes attempt maneuvers at speeds and altitudes that could cause a crash.
[/list]

In addition, there has also been a number of other issues and minor improvements:
[list]
[*] The enemy offscreen direction arrows are now brighter, and resize based on the distance from the player.
[*] The scoring system around shooting accuracy has been changed to fix the case where you complete the mission without firing a shot. Accuracy is now just a bonus, and is no longer multiplied by the score. This should result in higher mission scores.
[*] Crashing into soldiers no longer stops or bounces the player aircraft.
[*] Shooting off the wing, or any other part of an AI aircraft will immediately credit you with the victory to ensure that another aircraft doesn't continue to attack the tumbling aircraft and steal the victory.
[*] Crash landing upside down should now end the game with a "crash landed" result.
[*] The bombs on the Bristol F.2 are no longer left suspended in mid air when the aircraft loses a wing.
[/list]

notes.title: December 2024 Update
notes.content:
Welcome to the December 2024 update for Blue Sky Aces, a low poly WW1 flight simulator. It's been a couple of months since my last update so there's a couple of great new features to talk about, plus an update on the simulation flight model.

The first great new feature added is damage visual effects on aircraft, vehicles, and balloons, which simulate bullet holes. This is something that's been sitting in the backlog for a long time, until I discovered a great tutorial to turn simple cubes into tiny decal projectors using a clever shader.

The next awesome feature is head tracking, which allows you to look around while flying in first person view in a really natural way, that makes you feel like you're almost in the cockpit. Check out this tutorial that teaches you how to set it up with nothing more than a standard web camera: [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGoRnmXEXYQ]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGoRnmXEXYQ[/url]

Phase one of the simulation flight model is nearly complete, and I'm really hopeful that an update containing all of the above will be released early in January. Until then you can check out the progress in the video below:
[previewyoutube=OffbpXf1Z64;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Demo Update - New Map and Missions
notes.content:
The 0.86.33 demo update adds a new fighter sweep mission based on a brand new map, with the ability to select which aircraft you want to fly against. This map has improved scenery, and has been optimized to allow for more units of all types.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44495789/50614a24728e2cf061b3f5f87bfc73ae852a87fb.jpg[/img]

[h2]Aircraft Improvements[/h2]
The aircraft and their flight models have had a number of improvements such as:
[list]
[*] Better take off and landing characteristics, which are supported by more appropriately sized airfields.
[*] Minor improvements to the aircraft engine and wheel animations.
[*] The aircraft performance characteristics have been updated to be more realistic.
[*] The stall and gliding physics has been improved.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44495789/339d6e002cbb48190d7863cd6385aa32b1db1761.jpg[/img]

[h2]Updated Soldier Models[/h2]
The soldier models have been completely redesigned to better match the games aesthetic, and there are now multiple variations for each side including infantry, officers, pilots, and mechanics.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44495789/29fbd8e785dac31820830a6b9dca4806dbd5b0fe.jpg[/img]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed various Spanish translations.
[*] Fixed an issue where trains would attempt to derail themselves at certain intersections and stations.
[*] Fixed an issue where bullets would sometimes pass through soldiers without hitting them.
[*] Third person camera fixes when looking straight up or down, where the camera would flip around the vertical axis.
[*] The AI aircraft's ability to avoid collisions with the ground and balloons has been greatly improved.
[*] Fixed an issue where the player aircraft and aiming cross-hair would stutter every 2000 meters.
[*] Balloons no longer explode when you collide with them, instead they should burn down to the ground before exploding. The soldiers in observation balloons can now be shot.
[*] Stopped the aiming cross-hair from jumping around when the aim assistant is off, and the cross-hair is moving over a target aircraft.
[/list]

notes.title: Demo Update 0.86.29
notes.content:
The 0.86.29 build of the demo addresses a number of issues identified over the last couple of weeks that were affecting some players.
[list]
[*] Mouse movement issues at high frame rates have been fixed. This issue usually occurred when the v-sync was disabled, or when running on the low, or very low graphics setting.
[*] Issues saving the invert axis option on control bindings has been fixed. In addition a "save" button has been added to the control binding dialog, which makes it possible to change this option without changing the bound control.
[*] Improvements have been made to the AI aircraft head on avoidance logic to reduce the likelihood of them hitting each other, or the player's aircraft.
[*] A troubleshooting section has been added to the settings screen to help detect the source of input control issues, by making it easy to identify which devices are generating unwanted input. This screen also provides the ability to disable input from devices that are causing problems.
[/list]

notes.title: Demo Update - New preferences screen, and improved AI
notes.content:
The 0.86.26 demo update includes the addition of a new preferences screen, which provides for more customization of the game. The aircraft AI has also been reworked to make enemies more aggressive, and to improve their aiming to make them more deadly.

[b]Here's the full list of the improvements:[/b]
[list]
[*]  The aircraft maneuvering and aiming AI has been improved, and they now lead the target.
[*]  You can now configure the first and third person camera field of views.
[*]  Change how the look controls work in first person mode.
[*]  Define the visibility of various heads-up display elements.
[*]  Configure weapon options such as how rockets are fired, and the delay on bomb fuses.
[*]  Zoom is now available in first and third person modes. By default the 'V' key, left gamepad stick push, joystick button 6, and middle mouse buttons toggle zoom, but you can customize all except the mouse via the controls screen.
[*]  Added a "look back" function to allow you to quickly check behind you with a single button press. By default hold the '.' key, D-Pad down, or joystick button 7.
[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] The stuttering and jittering of other aircraft has been significantly reduced. The game in general should look much smoother now.
[*] Aircraft landings are now more realistic, as the automatic brakes are no longer applied until your aircraft slows right down.
[*] You can now fire your guns after your aircraft has lost it's engine power.
[*] Improvements have been made to font handling to reduce the likelihood of missing characters for languages with large character sets such as Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
[*] Fixed an issue where an aircraft could continue to fly after losing all or part of its tail.
[*] A damaged engine now has less power, which will reduce an aircraft's top speed.
[/list]

notes.title: Demo Update - New Aircraft & Missions
notes.content:
The 0.86.16 demo update adds a new progression system that allows you to unlock all 6 demo aircraft, and play new missions. The progression system is a simplified version of what will be in the full game, tailored to the content available in the demo. The way the progression system works is you start at the beginning of the war, and as you complete missions you progress through the war's timeline, whereby new aircraft become available based on the date they first entered service. Missions are also unlocked in the same way.

Here's a full list of new features:
[list]
[*]  Added the ability to fly all of the aircraft that you can see in the menu once they're unlocked.
[*]  Included additional missions for both sides that can be unlocked as you progress throughout the war's timeline.
[*]  There is now a progression system based on the war's timeline, as you complete missions and earn points you'll progress through the war, which will unlock aircraft and missions.
[*]  Added language support for Ukrainian.
[*]  Minor aircraft model improvements to the cockpits.
[*]  Added joystick and gamepad look support to the third person view, and smoothed out the look reset to be less jarring. As part of this work I've removed extra side and front third person cameras as they are no longer required.
[/list]

notes.title: Demo Update - Target Lead Indicator
notes.content:
The latest demo update (version 0.86.13) contains some great improvements for helping to target enemy aircraft, and an aiming assistant mode to make it easier and fairer for players using controllers. The target lead indicator has no impact on your score, however the aiming assistant will reduce your score by 25%. Both these options are configurable from the mission briefing screen so give them a try and let me know what you think about them.

In addition there's also a number of great improvements based on player feedback:
[list]
[*] Machine gun bullets now have a random spread which makes them look better, and has the side effect of making it slightly easier to hit the targets.
[*] New messages have been added to indicate when you hit or destroy an enemy target.
[*] I've increased the aircraft pitch rate to make it easier to turn and loop. 
[/list]
There's also several minor bug fixes:
[list]
[*] Fixed the smoke effects for the player aircraft that were playing in local space instead of world space.
[*] Added extra checks to prevent the game controller haptics (vibrations) continuing during a weapon reload.
[*] Fixed an issue where AI aircraft were sometimes not following their flight plan.
[*] Improvements to the AI aircraft turning when being pursued to remove some of the unnecessary pitch changes that were making it hard to stay on target.
[/list]
Finally I'd like to thank everyone who provided feedback, either here on Steam, or on other platforms, it's been absolutely awesome and I really appreciate it, and I feel it's make a huge difference to the game. Feel free to keep posting your feedback and I'll see what I can get done.  I've already got some further changes planned for the very near future which I think people will like, so keep watching to find out what they are.

notes.title: Demo Update - Controller and Camera Improvements
notes.content:
The latest demo update contains changes to improve Joystick and Gamepad handling, and camera following based on feedback received.

The Joystick change addresses two issues, which will also benefit Gamepads. The first was to make the stick less sensitive near the center to make it easier to make fine adjustments when trying to aim. The second was to address an issue whereby it wasn't possible to apply full elevator and aileron at the same time, as the input system was normalizing the input values restricting the values to 70% of their maximum when the stick was moved diagonally. These two changes should provide better maneuverability and finer grained control, but I'd like to hear your feedback on whether these changes have made a difference so please leave a comment below.

The other change involved removing the chase camera dead zone, and reducing the soft zone and damping to ensure the player aircraft stays more central in the screen.

notes.title: Demo Update - Joystick Binding Issues
notes.content:
The demo has been updated to address issues some users were experiencing when trying to configure flight simulator devices such as joysticks, throttles, and rudder pedals. All these devices are generally treated as joysticks by the input system, which was causing conflicts when trying to configure multiple devices to use at the same time. The symptoms of the issue were that a function on one device would trigger its configured function, as well as a second unintended function, for example a throttle which also adjusts the rudder.

The control rebind screen now has an extra option called "Generalize Control Path" which can be used to control whether a device input is bound to all similar devices, or a specific device. When setting up multiple flight simulator devices it is recommended to uncheck this option which will cause the action to be bound to a specific device. It is also recommended to rebind all flight controls with this option unchecked, even the ones that work, as this will ensure that all controls are bound to specific devices only. A control binding now turns yellow when it has been altered, so ensuring that all control bindings are yellow is an easy way of ensuring that they have all been rebound.

In addition I've also modified the way the aircraft identification boxes work within the game, enemy aircraft now have red boxes and identification text, and friendly aircraft are blue. The offscreen direction indicator arrows for enemy aircraft are also red, however they no longer show for friendly aircraft to make it easier to follow an enemy when it has left your field of view.

notes.content:
In this development log I cover work towards preparing a demo build for release later this year. notes.title: September Development Update
notes.content:
The last month since announcing the game has been spent getting the Steam integration completed, this is now done so the focus shifts to polishing the game for a demo release. The goal is to get a free demo ready in the fourth quarter of 2023, hopefully mid to late October. I haven't finalized the exact content for the demo yet but it's likely to include one British and one German aircraft, and between 4 and 6 set piece missions.

From now on I'm aiming to provide weekly updates on the progress, as well as providing some sneak peaks at what I'm working on. This week the focus is on adding damage zones to aircraft to make shooting accuracy more important. The idea is pretty simple, shooting the important parts like the engine do more damage than hitting the fabric covered wings or fuselage. The other benefit of this is that it allows for different damage effects to be shown to give the player a visual indicator of their shooting accuracy. I'll post some video of the new effects in my next update.
